**Partial fractions.** Let $g(x) = (2025+x)\ln(2025+x)$. Since $(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$ has simple roots,
- $A = g(1)/((1-2)(1-3)) = 2026\ln 2026/2 = 1013\ln 2026$
- $B = g(2)/((2-1)(2-3)) = -2027\ln 2027$
- $C = g(3)/((3-1)(3-2)) = 1014\ln 2028$

All three match the proposed solution.

**Expansions around $0$.**
- $\frac{1}{x-1} = -\sum_{n\ge 0} x^n$
- $\frac{1}{x-2} = -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{n\ge 0} \frac{x^n}{2^n}$
- $\frac{1}{x-3} = -\frac{1}{3}\sum_{n\ge 0} \frac{x^n}{3^n}$

So the coefficient of $x^n$ is
$$d_n = -1013\ln 2026 + \frac{2027\ln 2027}{2^{n+1}} - \frac{1014\ln 2028}{3^{n+1}}.$$

The last two terms vanish as $n\to\infty$, so $\lim_{n\to\infty} d_n = -1013\ln 2026$.

**Numerical check.** $\ln 2026 \approx 7.6138186847$, so $1013 \ln 2026 \approx 7712.7983276$, which agrees with the stated value $-7712.798327711141$ to about eight significant figures.
